deadline.value: Apply by February 1, 2027 for September 2027; meeting this deadline also makes you eligible for major awards.

also.quote: Students who meet these deadlines will be eligible for consideration for any major awards and scholarships

gre_general.value: The GRE General test is not required.
gre_general.quote: The GRE and the GRE subject area test in Chemistry and/or Biochemistry are not required.

gre_subject.value: The GRE Chemistry subject test is not required.
gre_subject.quote: The GRE and the GRE subject area test in Chemistry and/or Biochemistry are not required.

toefl_min.value: TOEFL 4.5 on the new 1-6 scale, with 5 in writing and speaking.

ielts_min.value: IELTS Academic 7.0 overall with at least 6.5 in writing and speaking.

supervisor.value: You do not need a supervisor to apply, but an offer depends on an appropriate research advisor being available, so look for one among the faculty.
supervisor.quote: offers of admission depend on other factors, including the availability of an appropriate research advisor | Read about our research faculty and find a research supervisor.

funding.value: Every full-time PhD student, international included, gets at least CAD 29,145 a year for four years; internationals also get an award covering the international tuition difference.
funding.quote: Full-time doctoral students (both domestic and international) receive minimum funding of $29,145 per year (effective May 1, 2026) for up to four years.

also.quote: International students in a full-time PhD program will be awarded an International Doctoral Student Award (IDSA)

entry_route.value: A master's in science with 75% is the normal route; direct entry from a BSc needs about 89% overall.
entry_route.quote: A Master of Science (MSc) degree (or equivalent) in Science with at least a minimum overall standing of 75% | Direct admission to the PhD program from a Bachelor of Science (BSc) program is also possible for outstanding students who graduated with an overall 89% standing

notes: Run jointly with the University of Guelph through the Guelph-Waterloo Centre for Graduate Work in Chemistry and Biochemistry (GWC2).
